newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Japan index sheds 10.9 percent in January - MSCI.
newsitem.headline: Japan index sheds 10.9 percent in January - MSCI.

text.p: Japanese stocks continued to decline in January, with Morgan Stanley Capital International's Japan index losing 10.9 percent in the month, MSCI said on Tuesday.

Mounting concern about the nation's banks, particularly their vulnerability to non-performing real estate loans, contributed to Japan putting in the weakest performance of any market -- developed or emerging -- for the month, MSCI said.
Japan was the worst performing stock market in 1996.
MSCI said two major shocks accounted for a 22.6-percent decline in the banking index in January.

Mitsubishi Trust & Banking sharply cut its profit forecast for the current fiscal year while Moody's Investors Service Inc downgraded the credit rating outlook for four medium-sized banks to negative from stable, citing the Japanese government's reluctance to bail out distressed lenders.
A weak economy, a lack of progress on economic policy reform and no signals from the government that it will intervene to cushion the market's decline contributed to the sell-off in Japan, MSCI said.
The MSCI world index of 22 developed stock markets gained 1.1 percent in January while the EAFE (Europe, Australasia, Far East) index fell 3.6 percent.
The MSCI emerging markets free index surged 6.7 percent with double-digit gains recorded in nine different countries.
The MSCI all country world index free, comprising both developed and emerging markets, gained 1.5 percent in January.
Among the strongest developed markets were Italy, the United States and Finland. Weakest performers were Japan, Australia and Austria.
Among emerging markets, Turkey led all performers with a 52.6 percent advance in January. Russia and Hungary also showed momentum.
Weakest emerging markets in January were Thailand, Venezuela and China Free, MSCI said.
